headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend holds, but hot US inflation cools the week

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with medium confidence (65/100), so this is still a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because the short-term mood has cooled after hot US inflation data, price is resting right on its 50-day average, and the Fed meets on 27 October, grow the budget in steps rather than all at once and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $81,233. This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

reasons: Price is 13% above its 200-day average and up 28% over 90 days.
About 64% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average.
Price sits less than 1% above its 50-day average ($81,233), below the $86,603 30-day high.
The 200-day average still slopes down (-1%) and price is 34% below its record.
watch: The longer picture leans up, but hot US inflation has raised the odds of a Fed rate rise on 27 October while price sits less than 1% above its 50-day average ($81,233). A close below that line would test the uptrend; calmer Fed signals and a move back above $86,603 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still points up, but this week the mood has cooled. Short term, things lean slightly cautious: US inflation came in hotter than expected at 3.7% and the odds of a Fed rate rise this month roughly doubled (PANews), which is nudging the mood down, and big Bitcoin funds saw about $487M leave in a single day. A close above $86,603 (the 30-day high) would turn this clearly up, a close below $81,233 (the 50-day average) turns it down, and in between expect choppy moves, with price now less than 1% above that lower line. Calmer inflation news or fund money returning would firm this up; for now steady, trust-first messaging fits better than urgent pushes.

Over the next month the picture still leans up with real strength: Bitcoin is about 28% higher than three months ago, and about 64% of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average. Fewer people than usual are betting on a rise with borrowed money, so the climb does not look overstretched. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high), while the move fades if it slips below $81,233 (the 50-day average), which is very close to today's $81,802. The Fed decides on 27 October, so a rate rise there would weaken this lean, while a pause would support growth campaigns aimed at active traders.

On the 3-6 month view the recovery is intact but still young: price is about 13% above its 200-day average, though that average still slopes down slightly and Bitcoin is 34% below its record. Bank adoption news is adding a little: Standard Chartered started licensed Bitcoin and Ether trading for wealthy clients in the UAE, and Kraken agreed to buy an EU bank (both via PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,287 (the 200-day average), with $66,506 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. The 200-day average turning upward would strengthen this; for the business it supports steady investment in onboarding rather than short bursts.

team_notes.marketing: Keep growing, but in steps: the longer picture leans up while the short-term mood has cooled and no rally or drop window is open, so run steady campaigns for active traders rather than urgent pushes. Make this week's content about explaining what US inflation and the Fed meeting mean for crypto.

items.why: Several large exchanges are growing products that let users trade crypto tokens tied to US stocks. Bybit announced mStocks with Mantle, Binance said its bStocks holdings passed $888 million and can now be used as collateral, OKX added stock-linked contracts, and Nasdaq-listed Perpetuals.com plans a tokenized stock venue under the SEC's innovation exemption.
items.marketing_angle: A timely education topic for users curious about stocks and crypto in one app.

sources.title: Bybit to Launch Tokenized Stock Product mStocks in Partnership with Mantle
Binance bStocks AUM surpasses $888 million, collateral feature further opened to all users
Perpetuals.com, led by former FTX Europe head, plans to launch tokenized US stock trading platform

items.why: The European Banking Authority named USDC the first 'significant' e-money token under the EU's MiCA rules, bringing tighter oversight, and the Dutch central bank licensed a planned euro stablecoin issuer. Polygon finished buying US payments firm Coinme, gaining money-transfer licences in most states, while Standard Chartered pushed back its forecast for the stablecoin market reaching $2 trillion to 2030.
items.marketing_angle: Good material for a plain explainer on how stablecoins are regulated and why that matters for users.

items.theme: Crypto stocks and altcoins slide after inflation data
items.why: After the hotter-than-expected US inflation report, US stocks closed lower and crypto-linked shares fell hard: MARA and Riot dropped about 10%, Robinhood about 9% and Strategy about 6%. Most large altcoins also slipped, with Ether down about 3% on the day; the reports tie the drop to the inflation data but don't give a clearer reason for the size of the moves.
items.marketing_angle: Expect more questions from active traders; calm, explanatory content fits better than promotions this week.
